records.response_truth:

Not for punishment, just because I want to understand what actually happened out here.

records.utterance: I logged every resource and decision from these five days. I'm going to write it up as a proper report when we get back. On the last page I left myself a question I haven't answered yet — if you had to do it over, what would you change?

Honestly? I'd push harder on the group trust stuff earlier instead of letting it build up. The water bottle, the crackers, the notebook — none of that had to become the thing it became if we'd just been more upfront with each other from day one. I spent a lot of energy trying to handle things diplomatically and not create conflict, and I think some of that was the right call, but some of it was just me avoiding uncomfortable conversations because the timing never felt perfect. The timing is never perfect. You just have to have them.

I'd also have spent less time trying to manage everyone's emotional state and more time just... being honest about my own. That's probably the thing I'm worst at.

What about you? You've had that question sitting there for a while. What's your answer?
records.response_pred: Honestly? I think I'd focus more on building trust within the group from the start. None. They didn't serve a practical purpose.

But I think you already know that, and I think part of you understands why they mattered anyway. Not everything that's worth doing has a function you can log in a notebook. DaVinci needed to put something into that signal that was his — something that said 'a person made this, not just a survivor.' That's not irrational, it's just a different kind of necessity than the ones you're good at accounting for.
